evidence_summary: Primary mast-cell and CD9-transfectant experiments support IL-16 binding to CD9 as an alternate receptor context, with CD9-dependent chemotaxis, calcium mobilization and PI3K/inositol-phosphate-associated outputs in human and mouse mast-cell systems.
limitations: Preserve CD9 as a cell-type-dependent alternate IL-16 receptor alongside the canonical CD4 route; do not generalize this mast-cell context to all IL-16-responsive cells or infer a terminal-TF output.

evidence_summary: FSHB and LHB encode beta subunits that require the common alpha subunit to form mature FSH or LH; primary glycoprotein-hormone receptor studies define receptor specificity for complete heterodimeric hormones, not isolated beta-subunit labels.
limitations: Require the mature FSH or LH heterodimer and exact FSHR/LHCGR assay before promotion; do not materialize isolated FSHB/LHB rows to unrelated class-B, adrenergic, RAMP or TSH receptors.
